content.text: FacebookLog InLog InForgot Account?National Domestic Violence Hotline's PostNational Domestic Violence Hotline Verified accountFebruary 8, 2020 · Shared with PublicEmotional abuse can be just as hurtful as physical abuse. You may be in an emotionally/verbally abusive relationship if your partner:Calls you names or insults youTries to isolate you from friends or familyThreatens to hurt you, your children, your pets, or your familyRefuses to trust you and acts jealous or possessiveAttempts to control what you wearOr gaslights you.No one deserves to experience abuse of any kind, for any reason. If you have concerns about what’s happening in your relationship, contact us by calling 1-800-799-SAFE (7233) or 1-800-787-3224 TTY, or chat online at www.thehotline.org.Learn more warning signs at: http://bit.ly/2m1oM7zAll reactions:23425 comments206 sharesLikeCommentMost relevant Susan AndersonAnd Physical Abuse ALWAYS includes EMOTIONAL Abuse!!! Living every second of the day in fear for your life, is the ultimate emotional abuse!!!!6y13View 1 replySusan AndersonI think we should not compare 1 form of abuse to another. They are all terrible to endure!!!! For over 20 years I endured a COMBINATION of emotional abuse, physical abuse, sexual abuse, and financial abuse by my ex. I think many victims will endure more than 1 form of abuse at a time. My ex would get drunk, verbally and emotionally abuse me for hours, and when those forms of abuse didn't "CONTROL" me like he wanted, he would physically abuse me!!!! In hindsight, I don't think I noticed how the emotional abuse was wearing me down!!! I was beginning to question my own perception of the dangerous reality that surrounded me. I became an angry, depressed person... a person I didn't want to be!!! I was just EXISTING, NOT LIVING!!! Getting out of this abusive relationship was the hardest thing I've ever done, but the BEST thing I have ever done!!!6y5View 1 replyJeanette Friari have nightmares still n i cant sleep i frightened of going out incase he there i dont wanna stay in coz i get anxious and stressed out i try push my self n i go out i listen to music n am in my own world but soon as it gone i stressed out what i have been threw gave me all the emotions that domestic abuse has my self confidence has gone my mojo has gone this person i fell for big time and he didnt just break me and my heart he ripped my heart out i cant trust no one not even my self i am trying hard to fix myself and its really hard to do but anno it will take a long time but i will try get there6y2View all 8 repliesKim CowherdI’m a 28 year survivor but I still have triggers....6yLisa Starsinic GilmoreMore often than not, it’s worse.6yCarmen SantiagoIt can be worse than physical abuse....6yBenavieri Counseling & CoachingThis is so important to acknowledge. The absence of physical violence does NOT mean that domestic violence isn’t happening in someone’s home. I hear so often from clients that “it isn’t that big of a deal” because they are not being physically threatened or hurt, but it IS a big deal if someone is being emotionally abused, those scars often take much longer to heal. I hope this message reaches women and men who don’t think they deserve help because of the non-“violent” nature of their abuse and gives them the courage to reach out!6yJen CrewThank you for the work you do, you are angels in disguise and I love you all; thank you.6yAnna YimWe don't have to live like this anymore. 6y1Barbara Fix GalloSAD....& very true!6y All reactions:23425 comments206 sharesLikeCommentMost relevant Susan AndersonAnd Physical Abuse ALWAYS includes EMOTIONAL Abuse!!!
